project.name: llava-for-sensors
project.description: Multimodal fault-prediction model fusing time-series sensor data with vision and language on a frozen Qwen2-VL-2B (LLaVA-for-sensors), trained locally on M2 Max.

nodes.name: AGENTS.md
nodes.summary: Operating contract for Codex exec workers (the bounded code-writers invoked by the implementer subagent): hard rules forbidding network access, git operations, scope drift, and invented domain content; plus learned-from-fan-in-misses UI/styling and test-value contracts.
nodes.languageNotes: Companion to CLAUDE.md; both files together define the director/implementer/codex three-role split that the write-scope-guard hook enforces.

nodes.name: CLAUDE.md
nodes.summary: Master operating contract for the Claude director agent: spec-authoring discipline, the production-realistic-not-deployed scope rule, autonomous-mode behavior, the per-packet build loop (Linear issue -> impl subagent -> codex exec -> Codex review gate -> head-pinned squash-merge), and Claude's own file-scope allowlist enforced by hooks/write-scope-guard.mjs.
nodes.languageNotes: Load-bearing; every section traces to a real past fan-in failure. This file is the source of truth for the director/impl/codex split that shapes every PR in the repo.

nodes.name: PLAN.md
nodes.summary: Planning contract for the project: pre-registered headline-figure design (3-bar modality ablation on CWRU bearing-fault classification, 5 seeds, 95% bootstrap CI, paired bootstrap p), framework choice (PyTorch + MPS, fp16, no 4-bit in v1), and an 8-phase delivery plan with per-phase code/data, LikeC4-view, /understand re-run, Linear subissue, and exit-gate specs.
nodes.languageNotes: Pre-registers the experimental acceptance criterion before any model code exists, including the negative-result protocol — a discipline borrowed from preregistered scientific studies.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Public-facing project overview: one-line thesis (sensors + vision + text beats vision + text on CWRU bearing-fault classification), reviewer entry-points table linking to PLAN/RUNNING_NOTES/TECH_REPORT/architecture/Linear, headline-figure and Gradio-demo placeholders to be filled in later phases, and the one-line doctrine statement.
nodes.languageNotes: Currently Phase-0 state — placeholders for headline SVG (Phase 4) and demo screenshot (Phase 5) are explicit and dated by phase deliverable.

nodes.name: RUNNING_NOTES.md
nodes.summary: Append-only lab journal: per-phase decisions, dead ends, blockers, tooling install state, and memory/timing measurements. Currently holds the Phase-0 provenance log (template instantiation, Linear hierarchy creation, codex-worker quota incident, zawarudo template-leak cleanup) and scheduled-but-empty headers for Phases 1-7.
nodes.languageNotes: Raw material from which TECH_REPORT.md is distilled in Phase 6; append-only discipline preserves an honest record of dead ends and reversed decisions.

nodes.name: TECH_REPORT.md
nodes.summary: Skeleton of the Phase-6 mini-arXiv writeup: abstract, related work, method (frozen Qwen2-VL-2B + LoRA + classification head + time-series encoder + fusion adapter), data (CWRU split + Phase-1 toy dataset), ablations (the pre-registered headline figure plus per-modality table), limitations, future work, reproducibility. Each section is currently a one-line stub describing what will land there.
nodes.languageNotes: Intentionally stub-only at Phase 0 — content is forbidden until Phase 6, since real content depends on Phase-4 ablation results.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: Minimal Node project manifest: pins likec4 ^1.57 as the only runtime dependency and exposes a single build:c4 script that compiles architecture/ LikeC4 source into docs/architecture/ exports. Marked private (never published).
nodes.languageNotes: Per the project's local-dev-only doctrine, package.json is for tooling only — no publish workflow, no semver discipline beyond initial 0.0.1.

nodes.name: pyproject.toml
nodes.summary: Python project manifest declaring requires-python >=3.11, runtime dependencies (torch>=2.4, transformers, peft, accelerate, numpy, pandas, matplotlib, gradio>=4.0), dev tools (pytest, ruff), uv-managed Python preference, and ruff config (py311 target, 100-col line length).
nodes.languageNotes: uv owns the Python toolchain per the 2026-05-26 user directive — system python3 is 3.10 on this M2 Max, so [tool.uv] python-preference = managed routes everything through uv's installed 3.12.

nodes.name: compaction-sidecar.sh
nodes.summary: Combined PreCompact/PostCompact Claude Code hook that writes durable breadcrumb JSON (resume-pointer.json, last-compaction.json) into .claude/hooks/ so a post-compaction SessionStart reflex can recover Linear project context and the latest git state. Always exits 0 to guarantee compaction is never blocked.
nodes.languageNotes: Bash wrapper that delegates JSON construction to an embedded python3 heredoc, deliberately passing the hook payload via the HOOK_IN env var (stdin is consumed by the heredoc itself) and using json.dump rather than shell interpolation to stay safe with branch/commit strings containing quotes.

nodes.name: delegation-sidecar.sh
nodes.summary: PostToolUse hook fired after every Edit/Write/MultiEdit that surfaces a soft, throttled (~5 min) operating-compass nudge reminding Claude of standing delegation-first, Linear-plans/GitHub-delivers principles, with an optional gentle aside when the edit touched implementation code. Fail-open and strictly non-fatal.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a jq-first / python3-fallback parser to read tool_input.file_path from the hook payload, skips re-entrant edits to hook files, throttles via a /tmp stamp file, and emits a hookSpecificOutput JSON envelope with additionalContext for Claude Code to inject.

nodes.name: session-recovery.sh
nodes.summary: SessionStart bash wrapper around session-recovery.py whose sole structural job is to guarantee the context-recovery reflex never silently vanishes: it invokes the python helper, and if python3 is missing or the helper errors, emits a hardcoded loud-degraded payload demanding a RESUME-ACK as the first output line. Explicitly skips recovery when source=clear.
nodes.languageNotes: Minimal bash shim that resolves its own directory via $(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd) to locate the sibling python helper, and uses an inline python3 -c snippet to safely parse the JSON source field rather than relying on shell substring matching.

nodes.name: check-prereqs.sh
nodes.summary: Verifies dev/build/test prerequisites (node, npm, uv, python3, git-lfs, likec4) at required versions and runs a regression check ensuring no runtime references to the stale .template.answers file exist in scripts/ or hooks/.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses portable POSIX awk for semver comparison (version_ge) so it works on macOS/BSD without GNU coreutils.

nodes.name: version_ge
nodes.summary: Compares two dot-separated version strings numerically using POSIX awk, tolerating non-numeric suffixes like '3.11.0rc1'. Returns exit 0 if X >= Y.

nodes.name: fail
nodes.summary: Prints a failure marker for a prerequisite check, optionally including an install hint, and increments fail_count for the final verdict.

nodes.name: check-shell-syntax.sh
nodes.summary: Runs `bash -n` syntax check against the STAGED blob (via `git show :FILE`) of all tracked shell scripts so the pre-commit hook validates exactly what will be committed, with a hint for the common python3 -c single-quote pitfall.
nodes.languageNotes: Validates the staged blob rather than the working tree, catching the common 'git add then fix' divergence bug.

nodes.name: codex-review.sh
nodes.summary: Pre-PR adversarial local review backstop: runs `codex exec` (gpt-5.5 / xhigh effort by default) read-only over the full git diff vs origin/main and emits a graded P0-P3 finding list with a strict pass/fail verdict, enforced as a required gate.
nodes.languageNotes: Feeds the prompt via stdin (not argv) to avoid Linux's ~131 KiB ARG_MAX limit on large diffs; refuses to silently partial-review when diffs exceed CODEX_REVIEW_MAX_BYTES.

nodes.name: codex-run.sh
nodes.summary: Dispatches a `codex exec` worker or explorer run inside .codex-runs/<run-id>/, capturing the full event stream, exit code, and git diff so Claude can audit Codex's edits; intent-adds only the delta of untracked files created during the invocation to make the audit-trail check defensible.
nodes.languageNotes: Closes stdin with </dev/null to prevent backgrounded codex runs from hanging on 'Reading additional input from stdin'.

nodes.name: codex-runs-gc.sh
nodes.summary: Garbage-collects .codex-runs/ artifact families with merged/gone protection: never deletes a run whose slug has an alive non-merged branch, never touches parallel-metrics.tsv, and groups child runs (-w0, -rev1, -fix1) into a single family for atomic deletion.
nodes.languageNotes: Includes a hermetic --self-test mode that builds a throwaway git repo with synthetic families and re-invokes itself to assert the merged/gone policy.

nodes.name: slug_protected
nodes.summary: Returns 0 (protected) if any local or origin ref matches the slug fragment AND that ref is NOT merged into origin/main — preserving live work from GC while allowing merged work to be collected.

nodes.name: base_of
nodes.summary: Strips child suffixes (-w0, -rev1, -fix1, -prepr, -selfreview) from a run id to derive the family base id, enabling per-family GC decisions instead of per-dir.

nodes.name: impl-precommit-scope.sh
nodes.summary: Authoritative two-layer scope gate enforcing both the per-packet allowlist (--scope-file) and the role allowlist (write-scope-guard.mjs) against staged (--cached) or committed (--base) diffs in an impl worktree, with fail-closed semantics and rename decomposition.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses --no-renames to decompose `git mv` into delete+add so both source and destination are validated, closing the rename-to-evade-scope hole. AGENT_TYPE is hard-coded (never sourced from worker-writable state) to prevent identity forgery.

nodes.name: in_packet_scope
nodes.summary: Returns 0 if a path matches an exact file entry or directory-prefix entry from the packet allowlist; guards array expansion under set -u and uses local-scoped loop vars to avoid clobbering the caller's $f.

nodes.name: review-gate.sh
nodes.summary: Canonical helper for the GitHub Codex review gate: status/threads (reads), reply/resolve (GraphQL mutations), and a two-phase eye-emoji `wait` loop that auto-posts `@codex review` on missed acks then polls for a head-pinned verdict, distinguishing CLEAN-REVIEW (auto-mergeable) from CLEAN-COMMENT-MANUAL (operator-confirm-required).
nodes.languageNotes: Matches both REST `chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]` and GraphQL `chatgpt-codex-connector` login forms; safe auto-clean requires `review.commit.oid == headRefOid`, never a clean comment alone.

nodes.name: worktree-new.sh
nodes.summary: Provisions a per-packet git worktree under <repo-parent>/.llava-for-sensors-worktrees/<name>/ with an APFS-cloned real node_modules (so the worktree is immediately bootable inside codex's workspace-write sandbox) and auto-wires the per-worktree pre-commit hook.
nodes.languageNotes: Refuses to provision off a possibly-stale base unless ALLOW_STALE_BASE=1 — fetches origin first and resolves BASE to a concrete SHA to prevent stale-base build failures and origin/main drift mid-run.

nodes.name: implementer.md
nodes.summary: The 383-line per-packet Impl Contract that the implementer subagent must follow end-to-end: cardinal rule (no direct code writes), path-scope contract, the nine-step pipeline from spec-read through codex-exec dispatch, local /codex:review gate, pre-PR notify, PR creation, eye-emoji review loop, and clean-verdict notify.
nodes.languageNotes: Load-bearing operating contract: codex is the only writer of production code, the impl orchestrates.

nodes.name: review-gate.md
nodes.summary: Slash-command definition that drives a PR through the Codex review gate to a clean head-pinned squash-merge, wrapping scripts/review-gate.sh wait/status/threads helpers.

nodes.name: work-issue.md
nodes.summary: Slash-command definition that takes a Linear issue from start to merged PR by dispatching the implementer subagent through the full build loop.

nodes.name: settings.json
nodes.summary: Claude Code project settings: permissions allowlist for non-destructive git/gh/codex/script commands, deny rules for force-push and dangerous flags, and PreToolUse/SessionStart/PreCompact/PostCompact/PostToolUse hooks wiring write-scope-guard.mjs, schedule-wakeup-guard.mjs, and session/compaction sidecars.
nodes.languageNotes: Hooks wire the PreToolUse write-scope guard that enforces Claude's file-scope contract.

nodes.name: DELEGATION.md
nodes.summary: The Claude-to-Codex-exec delegation doctrine: ownership boundaries, command modes (run vs task packet), trust-but-verify post-run audit, feedback loops, parallel strategy, and the cost/network policy enforced by .claude/settings.json deny rules.

nodes.name: codex-result.schema.json
nodes.summary: JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) defining the structured result every codex-exec worker must return: summary, files_inspected/changed, commands_run, verification_result, evidence, assumptions, risks, and follow-up flags.

nodes.name: task-template.md
nodes.summary: Canonical task.md template the implementer fills in for each codex-exec worker dispatch — context, deliverables, allowed-paths, verification commands, and the required structured-result envelope.

nodes.name: .template.answers
nodes.summary: Answers file consumed by the upstream orc-temp init.sh scaffolder — captures the project name, Linear prefix, branch prefix, Codex model selection, scope mode (blocklist), and the production-realistic deployment doctrine that drove CLAUDE.md generation.
nodes.languageNotes: PROJECT_NAME=zawarudo is the upstream template placeholder; the actual project slug llava-for-sensors lives in CLAUDE.md.

nodes.name: .understandignore
nodes.summary: Exclusion-pattern file for the understand-anything analyzer using gitignore syntax — all suggested patterns currently commented out so the full tree is analyzed.

nodes.languageNotes: LikeC4 DSL — extends the llava system defined in landscape.c4.

nodes.name: session-recovery.py
nodes.summary: SessionStart hook that injects a small context blob (cwd, transcript path, current branch and head SHA, ahead/behind counts vs origin/main) so resumed/compacted Claude sessions immediately know the worktree state.

nodes.name: _git
nodes.summary: Thin subprocess wrapper that runs a git command in the given cwd with a 5-second timeout and returns stripped stdout, swallowing errors so the hook never blocks the session.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Constructs the SessionStart additionalContext payload — collects cwd/transcript info plus current branch, head SHA, and ahead/behind tallies versus origin/main into the hookSpecificOutput envelope.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Hook entry point — reads the JSON payload from stdin, calls build() to assemble the recovery context, writes the response JSON to stdout.

nodes.name: pre-commit
nodes.summary: Worktree-scoped pre-commit hook installed by scripts/worktree-new.sh into each impl worktree — resolves the main repo root, runs impl-precommit-scope.sh against the staging area, then check-shell-syntax.sh on staged shell files.
nodes.languageNotes: Bash script with `set -euo pipefail`; delegates to canonical scripts in the main repo so worktrees stay clean.

nodes.name: write-scope-guard.mjs
nodes.summary: The 511-line PreToolUse hook that enforces the CLAUDE.md file-scope contract on Edit/Write/MultiEdit calls — distinguishes Claude (allowed only in .claude/.codex/hooks/docs/scripts/architecture/.understand-anything plus markdown/test files plus root .gitignore) from impl subagents (allowed anywhere inside a trusted linked worktree), denies otherwise with an explicit error pointing to the implementer subagent.
nodes.languageNotes: ES module with anchored path matching (path.resolve + prefix check, never substring) to defeat lenient bypasses called out in CLAUDE.md §recurring-failure-classes.

nodes.name: isInside
nodes.summary: Anchored containment check — returns true only when candidate's path.relative to root is a non-absolute, non-parent-traversal prefix; rejects substring matches.

nodes.name: findGitRoot
nodes.summary: Walks upward from a starting directory looking for a .git entry and returns the containing directory; falls back to null when none is found.

nodes.name: realpathOrNull
nodes.summary: Safe wrapper around fs.realpathSync that returns null instead of throwing when the path does not exist or cannot be resolved.

nodes.name: realpathOfPathOrParent
nodes.summary: Realpath-resolution helper that handles symlinked leaf paths and missing leaf files by walking up to the nearest extant ancestor, preserving the not-yet-created tail components.

nodes.name: canonicalAgentType
nodes.summary: Normalizes raw subagent type strings into the canonical implementer/explorer/main identifiers used by the deny/allow logic.

nodes.name: linkedGitdir
nodes.summary: Reads a worktree's .git pointer file and returns the absolute gitdir path it points to (or null when the entry is a real .git directory rather than a worktree link).

nodes.name: linkedWorktreeRootFromGitdir
nodes.summary: Given a worktree gitdir, parses the gitdir file to derive and realpath-resolve the worktree's working-tree root, validating the trailing /.git relationship.

nodes.name: trustedLinkedWorktree
nodes.summary: Validates that a candidate path is a real linked git worktree whose gitdir lives inside the main repo's .git/worktrees — the cryptographic anchor for impl-subagent trust.

nodes.name: resolveWriteRoot
nodes.summary: Core dispatcher that decides which root a write is bounded to based on the calling agent (main Claude vs impl subagent), TRUSTED_WORKTREE_ROOT env, and the hook cwd — returns the resolved root or null to deny.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker for the models/ container — placeholder awaiting the ts_encoder, fusion adapter, and Qwen2-VL-2B+LoRA+head modules from Phases 1-3.

nodes.name: pre-commit
nodes.summary: Main-repo pre-commit hook auto-wired by init.sh via `git config core.hooksPath scripts/hooks` — runs scripts/check-shell-syntax.sh against staged shell files only, exiting non-zero on any syntax failure.
nodes.languageNotes: POSIX /bin/sh with set -eu; uses xargs -0 to pipe NUL-delimited staged paths.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start at the README to absorb the thesis in one page: a frozen Qwen2-VL-2B with a small trainable fusion adapter that lets time-series sensor data flow into a vision-language model's token space — LLaVA, but for sensors. The thesis is measurable: sensors + vision + text must beat vision + text alone on CWRU bearing-fault classification across four classes, trained end-to-end on an M2 Max. The README also names the four reviewer entry-points (PLAN, RUNNING_NOTES, TECH_REPORT, architecture) that the next steps of this tour will visit in order.

tour.title: The Pre-Registered Headline Figure
tour.description: PLAN.md is the experimental contract: before any model code exists, it pre-registers the headline figure as a 3-bar modality ablation (text-only vs vision+text vs sensors+vision+text) with 5 seeds, 95% bootstrap confidence intervals, and a paired bootstrap p-value. This is the highest-fan-in document in the repo (4 inbound edges) — every other doctrine doc cross-references it. The 8-phase delivery plan that follows binds each phase to concrete exit gates, locking the build loop to a falsifiable scientific claim.
tour.languageLesson: Pre-registration is a discipline borrowed from clinical trials: you commit to the analysis (test, sample size, decision rule) BEFORE seeing data. It defeats p-hacking and HARKing (Hypothesizing After Results are Known) by removing the researcher's degrees of freedom retrospectively.

tour.title: The Director's Operating Contract
tour.description: CLAUDE.md is the master operating contract for the agent system that builds this project. Its central claim: Claude (the director) does not write production code — every production change flows through a per-packet implementer subagent that dispatches codex exec workers, with a per-PR audit trail. The doc encodes the production-realistic-not-deployed scope rule (single env, no infra automation, no backwards-compat shims), autonomous-mode behavior, and the build loop that ties Linear (planning ledger) to GitHub (delivery ledger). AGENTS.md is its sibling: the symmetric contract for the codex workers at the bottom of the stack.

tour.title: System Landscape (Architecture-as-Code)
tour.description: Architecture is checked in as source, not as drift-prone diagrams. landscape.c4 declares the system boundary in LikeC4 DSL — three actors (researcher/reviewer, the external CWRU bearing dataset, and the llava-for-sensors black box) and the relations between them. The .mmd file beside it is the Mermaid rendering that gets embedded in README and TECH_REPORT, generated by `npm run build:c4`. The pattern: one source of truth (.c4), many derived views (.mmd, .svg).
tour.languageLesson: LikeC4 implements the C4 model (Context / Containers / Components / Code) as a typed DSL with extends/inheritance. A landscape view defines the outermost ring; container views drill in. The whole graph is type-checked, so a renamed container fails the build everywhere it's referenced.

tour.title: Container Decomposition
tour.description: container.c4 zooms inside the llava-for-sensors system box from Step 4 and decomposes it into seven containers: data_pipeline, ts_encoder, fusion, vlm (the frozen Qwen2-VL-2B + LoRA + head), train_loop, eval_harness, and demo_app. The file has the highest fan-out in the entire graph (7) because it documents every Python package scaffold in the repo (data/, models/, train/, eval/, demo/). The three relation sets — training-time, eval-time, demo-time — express that the same containers participate in different data flows depending on the phase.

tour.title: The Implementer Contract
tour.description: Where CLAUDE.md describes the director's behavior, implementer.md is the 383-line contract the impl subagent itself follows. The cardinal rule: the impl has no Edit/Write/MultiEdit tools — it can only commission codex exec workers to write code, then audit their diffs. The doc walks a nine-step pipeline from spec-read through the local /codex:review gate, pre-PR notify, PR creation, and the eye-emoji review loop with the GitHub Codex bot. The supporting templates — DELEGATION.md, task-template.md, codex-result.schema.json — define the exact shape of every worker dispatch and the structured envelope every worker must return.

tour.title: Write-Scope Enforcement (the Wall)
tour.description: Doctrine in a markdown file is advisory; this is the wall that makes it enforced. write-scope-guard.mjs is a 511-line PreToolUse hook wired by .claude/settings.json that intercepts every Edit/Write/MultiEdit call and denies it unless the resolved path falls inside the active write root for the calling agent. Claude is bounded to .claude/.codex/hooks/docs/scripts/architecture/.understand-anything plus markdown anywhere; impl subagents are bounded to a trusted linked git worktree validated cryptographically against the main repo's .git/worktrees pointer. The hook is what stops Claude from quietly editing production Python.
tour.languageLesson: Anchored path matching: path.resolve() canonicalizes (collapsing `..`) BEFORE prefix-check, and matching uses strict prefix-from-root (`rel === p || rel.startsWith(p + '/')`) rather than substring-anywhere. This defeats the bypass `src/components/scripts/evil.ts` passing as 'scripts/'. The hook also realpath-resolves to defeat symlink chicanery — both lexical and realpath containment must succeed.

tour.title: The Orchestration Rails
tour.description: These four scripts are the rails the impl subagent runs on. worktree-new.sh provisions a per-packet sibling git worktree with an APFS-cloned node_modules so codex's sandbox boots instantly. codex-run.sh dispatches a worker into .codex-runs/<run-id>/ capturing the full event stream, exit code, and git diff for audit. impl-precommit-scope.sh is the two-layer scope gate — per-packet allowlist (--scope-file) on top of the role allowlist — that fails-closed on any path outside scope, including renames (decomposed via --no-renames). review-gate.sh wraps the GitHub Codex review bot in a head-pinned eye-emoji wait loop, distinguishing auto-mergeable CLEAN-REVIEW from operator-confirm-required CLEAN-COMMENT-MANUAL.
tour.languageLesson: Defense in depth, three layers: (1) the impl subagent's tools list strips Edit/Write/MultiEdit at the harness level, (2) write-scope-guard.mjs denies out-of-scope writes at PreToolUse, (3) impl-precommit-scope.sh fails the commit if anything still made it through. Each layer assumes the others may fail.

tour.title: Tooling and Dependencies
tour.description: pyproject.toml declares the Python runtime: requires-python >=3.11, torch>=2.4 for MPS-on-M2 training, plus transformers / peft / accelerate for the frozen-VLM-with-LoRA pattern, matplotlib for the headline figure, gradio for the Phase-5 demo, and pytest+ruff for dev. The [tool.uv] python-preference = managed line routes the toolchain through uv's installed Python 3.12 because system python3 is 3.10 on this M2 Max. package.json is intentionally minimal: likec4 is the only runtime dependency and the only script is build:c4 (no publish workflow, no semver — local-dev-only per the doctrine).
tour.languageLesson: uv is a Rust-written Python package manager that owns the interpreter as well as dependencies. `python-preference = managed` makes uv install its own Python rather than borrowing the system one, eliminating the M2 'system python3 is 3.10 but we need 3.11+' bootstrapping pain. requires-python in pyproject.toml is the upper bound that uv resolves against.

tour.title: The Production-Code Scaffold
tour.description: These five empty __init__.py files are the entire production-code surface at Phase 0. Each corresponds to one of the containers in Step 5's container.c4 diagram: data/ awaits the Phase-1 toy synthetic dataset then the CWRU loader, models/ awaits ts_encoder + fusion adapter + Qwen2-VL-2B+LoRA wiring across Phases 1-3, train/ awaits the headline ablation training loop (3 conditions × 5 seeds within 40 GB / 24 h on M2 Max), eval/ awaits the macro-F1 + bootstrap CI + paired-bootstrap-p logic, demo/ awaits the Gradio app. The emptiness is the point — every line that lands here goes through the codex exec audit trail you saw in Steps 6-8.

tour.title: Phase 0 Deliverables and the Path Forward
tour.description: Two append-only documents close the loop. RUNNING_NOTES.md is the lab journal — per-phase decisions, dead ends, blockers, timing measurements; right now it holds the Phase-0 provenance log (template instantiation, Linear hierarchy creation, codex-worker quota incident, template-leak cleanup) plus empty headers for Phases 1-7. TECH_REPORT.md is the mini-arXiv skeleton that will be distilled from RUNNING_NOTES in Phase 6: abstract, method, the pre-registered headline figure from Step 2, ablations, limitations, reproducibility. Each section is currently a one-line stub — intentionally, because real content depends on Phase-4 experimental results that haven't happened yet.
